issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the order-processing method in SealSaloon: the problem statement and UML specify a method named checkOrderReady() that should be called to attempt serving queued orders (see UML and textual description). The solution implementation provides a method named processOrders() (signature: public void processOrders()) and orderMeal() calls this.processOrders(). This divergent name for the same conceptual operation (attempting to serve/prepare queued orders) will confuse students who follow the specification and expect checkOrderReady(), and may cause tests or autograders that look for checkOrderReady() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation API match the problem statement: rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady() (change its declaration line and any internal calls), and have orderMeal() call checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders() so the method name required by the specification/UML exists and tests referencing checkOrderReady() succeed. Update documentation/comments to reflect the chosen name.

issues.description: Inconsistent instructions regarding the SealSaloon.stock attribute initialization: the problem text first instructs that the SealSaloon constructor (no-arg) should initialize default values ("These should be initialized ... in the constructor of SealSaloon"), but later explicitly requires that the stock attribute be static and final (shared across all instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is misleading and contradicts the later requirement that stock be static/final. The solution declares stock as a static final field initialized at declaration (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()).
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: state explicitly that orders should be initialized in the instance constructor, while the shared stock (static final) must be initialized at its declaration or in a static initializer. Remove or reword the sentence that instructs initializing the stock in the instance constructor to avoid implying a per-instance initialization. This preserves the intended design (single shared stock) and prevents student confusion about where to initialize a static final field.
